name: no IGST credit: CGST and SGST credit go against their own heads, IGST paid in cash
citation: CGST Act 2017 section 49(5)(b) and (c): central tax credit towards central tax, State tax credit towards State tax; neither can be used for the other

name: IGST credit first against IGST, the remainder against the head short of its own credit
citation: Rule 88A, CGST Rules 2017 (Notification 16/2019-Central Tax) and Circular 98/17/2019-GST: integrated tax credit first towards integrated tax, then towards central and State tax in any order and proportion

name: IGST credit must be used up before CGST or SGST credit, so own-head credit is carried forward
citation: CGST Act 2017 section 49A (inserted by the CGST (Amendment) Act 2018 from 01.02.2019) read with rule 88A: credit of central tax or State tax is utilised only after the integrated tax credit has been utilised fully

name: before February 2019 the original section 49(5) order applies
citation: CGST Act 2017 section 49(5)(a) as originally enacted: integrated tax credit first towards integrated tax and the amount remaining, if any, towards central tax and State tax

name: February and March 2019: the IGST remainder goes to CGST before SGST
citation: CGST Act 2017 section 49A in force from 01.02.2019 (Notification 2/2019-Central Tax) before rule 88A from 01.04.2019: the common portal applied the integrated tax remainder to central tax first

name: CGST and SGST credit each go against IGST after their own head
citation: CGST Act 2017 section 49(5)(b) and (c): central tax credit towards central tax then integrated tax; State tax credit towards State tax then integrated tax

name: CGST credit is never used for SGST, so it is carried forward while SGST is paid in cash
citation: CGST Act 2017 section 49(5)(e): the central tax shall not be utilised towards payment of State tax

name: paise are kept exact through the set-off
citation: Rule 88A: the integrated tax remainder may be applied to central and State tax in any proportion; here it goes to CGST, whose own credit of five paise then covers the rest

name: interest at 18 per cent a year for 15 days on the cash part
citation: CGST Act 2017 section 50(1) and Notification 13/2017-Central Tax: 18 per cent per annum; proviso to section 50(1) as substituted by Finance Act 2021 section 112: on the tax paid through the electronic cash ledger

name: no interest when paid on the due date
citation: CGST Act 2017 section 50(1): interest runs for the period for which the tax remains unpaid after the due date

name: GSTR-3B 15 days late, turnover one crore: fifty rupees a day under both Acts
citation: Notification 64/2017-Central Tax: twenty-five rupees a day under the CGST Act and the same under the State Act; Notification 19/2021-Central Tax: capped at one thousand rupees under each Act where the preceding year's aggregate turnover is up to one and a half crore rupees

name: GSTR-3B nil return 15 days late: twenty rupees a day
citation: Notification 64/2017-Central Tax: ten rupees a day under each Act where the central tax payable is nil; Notification 19/2021-Central Tax: capped at two hundred and fifty rupees under each Act for a nil return

name: GSTR-3B 60 days late, turnover one crore: capped at two thousand rupees
citation: Notification 19/2021-Central Tax: one thousand rupees under each Act where the aggregate turnover of the preceding financial year is up to one and a half crore rupees

name: GSTR-3B 60 days late, turnover three crore: capped at five thousand rupees
citation: Notification 19/2021-Central Tax: two thousand five hundred rupees under each Act where the aggregate turnover is above one and a half crore and up to five crore rupees

name: turnover not known: the highest cap is assumed and said so
citation: CGST Act 2017 section 47(1): five thousand rupees under each Act is the statutory maximum, which Notification 19/2021-Central Tax leaves for turnover above five crore rupees

name: May 2021 GSTR-3B before the 2021 caps: five thousand rupees under each Act
citation: Notification 19/2021-Central Tax applies to the tax period June 2021 onwards; before that section 47(1) caps the fee at five thousand rupees under each Act

name: August 2017 GSTR-3B: late fee waived
citation: Notification 50/2017-Central Tax dated 24.10.2017 waiving the late fee for FORM GSTR-3B of August and September 2017

name: GSTR-1 15 days late, turnover three crore
citation: Notification 4/2018-Central Tax: twenty-five rupees a day under each Act for FORM GSTR-1; Notification 20/2021-Central Tax: capped at two thousand five hundred rupees under each Act for turnover above one and a half crore and up to five crore rupees
